newsitem.title: JAPAN: DLR SLIGHTLY FIRMER IN TOKYO, BUT UPSIDE CAPPED.
newsitem.headline: DLR SLIGHTLY FIRMER IN TOKYO, BUT UPSIDE CAPPED.

text.p: 0145 GMT --*Dollar firmed slightly against yen in thin mid-morning Tokyo trade on Thursday due to purchases by interbank operators and yen selling against mark.
*Profit-taking interest blocked dollar before 116 yen, with U.S. fund operators also expected to sell on rallies.
*Mark firmed decisively above 63 yen due to possible purchases by Asian participants, but Japanese exporters' offers likely to block upside around 63.50 yen.
*Mark stood at 63.20/23 yen compared with 63.07 yen in New York on Wednesday.
*Day traders built some long positions in dollar after seeing firm bids by Japanese institutional investors lined up below 115.50 yen.
*Dollar mostly steady against yen in early Tokyo after earlier losses were offset by mark buying against yen in cross trade by Japanese operators.
*But traders keen to sell dollars on rises on perceptions that dollar's topside edging down and due to overnight falls particularly against mark, dealers said.

*Buying by Japanese investors expected to emerge at around 115.20-30 yen and below 115 yen, although their heavy purchases since earlier this week failed to lift dollar much due to active selling by U.S. funds operators, they said.
*"There is a sense that the dollar's ceiling is becoming lower and long positions have been squared," said a dealer at a U.S. bank.
*He said although Japanese life insurers bought dollars at below 115.50 yen overnight after heavy selling by U.S. funds at 115.90 yen, its recovery had been slow.
*Dollar's topside capped at around 115.80 yen after recovering from earlier low of 115.47 yen in early Asian trade.

*Dealer at U.S. bank said dollar may seek its floor against yen and mark in near term. Focus on release of Japan's customs-cleared trade data for July due out on Monday. *Reuters poll of economists produced average forecast of an 83 percent rise in its trade surplus from a year ago.
*Forecasts ranged from a 60 percent to a 114 percent increase in the surplus, or a surplus of 799 billion yen to 1.07 trillion yen.
